name: Estival-Nunatak
description: A single unbroken ocean swallows the horizon, its color shifting from wine-dark deeps to bright shelf-teal. The only interruptions are acid rain regions, breaking the swell in a ragged arc.

Standing still, you feel the temperate air press in like a verdict. Wind is the only voice here, and it repeats itself. Herds of six-limbed graziers shadow the meltwater margins, wary of anything that walks upright.
Geologists argue about the strata here: several layers appear deposited out of order, as if the planet's history were shuffled like cards.
The next expedition is already fitting out. Whether it returns with data, ore, or just debts depends on choices nobody has made yet.
